rounds.text: Kanpur Plastipack Ltd trades at an attractive P/E ratio of 11.2x on filed statements, offering a substantial discount relative to the sector benchmark P/E of 21.3x [E1, E6]. The company exhibits robust fundamental profitability, highlighted by an ROCE of 17.0% and an ROE of 14.9%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E8, E9, E10, E12, E13]. Operational momentum is accelerating, demonstrated by a 21% compounded sales growth in the trailing twelve months and a 53% surge in trailing profit growth [E16, E19]. Cash generation remains exceptionally strong, with a cash conversion ratio of 1.31x translating into ₹ 51 Cr of operating cash flow and ₹ 80 Cr of free cash flow in March 2026 [E31, E32, E33]. Valuation models suggest mispricing, as a reverse DCF indicates that today's market price merely prices in 0.2% earnings growth against a base-case expectation of 3.0%, while institutional interest is turning positive with domestic holdings rising to 1.68% alongside a high relative-strength rating of 94 [E40, E41, E44, E48]. Conceded: compounded profit growth over 5 years sits at a modest 3% and the 5-year median return on equity is restricted to 8% [E17, E24].

While recent trailing metrics look vibrant, the longer-term structural reality reveals a company weighed down by historically sluggish compounding and weak return profiles. Specifically, compounded profit growth over five years crawls at just 3% [E17], and the five-year compounded sales growth is flagged as poor at 9.77% [E56]. Furthermore, the longer-term return on equity paints a picture of mediocrity, with both 3-year and 5-year median ROE anchored at a low 8% [E24, E25, E57]. Compounding these operational hurdles, borrowings have surged significantly to Rs 163 Cr as of Sep 2026, up sharply from Rs 112 Cr a year prior [E36], coinciding with a warning flag that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E58]. Compounded by an annualized volatility of 51.5% [E51] and a worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -62.1% [E50], the stock exposes investors to severe turbulence that short-term momentum obscures. Conceded: [E19].

While the bear focuses on historical five-year metrics like the 3% profit growth [E17] and 9.77% sales growth [E56], it completely ignores the explosive acceleration happening right now, evidenced by trailing twelve-month sales growth of 21% [E16] and profit growth of 53% [E19]. Conceded: [E17, E56]. Similarly, while the median historical ROE of 8% [E24, E25] points to past mediocrity, the company has broken out of that band with a recent ROE of 14.71% against a sector benchmark of 10.88% [E9], alongside a surging TTM median ROE of 15% [E26]. The concern over rising borrowings to Rs 163 Cr [E36] is countered by the massive ₹ 80 Cr in free cash flow generated in March 2026 [E33] and a robust cash conversion ratio of 1.31x proving profits are fully backed by cash [E31]. That capital expenditure phase, visible in the +411.1% surge in CWIP [E37], shows that the increased leverage is funding active growth rather than masking structural decay. Finally, pointing to high historical volatility [E51] and drawdowns [E50] ignores the present reality that the stock carries a stellar 94 relative strength rating against the Nifty 500 [E48] and trades at an attractive P/E of 11.2 [E1] that sits well below sector benchmarks [E6].

While the bull highlights trailing twelve-month sales growth of 21% [E16] and profit growth of 53% [E19] to dismiss past mediocrity, it glosses over the fundamental reality that 5-year compounded profit growth sits at a meager 3% [E17] and 5-year sales growth is flagged as a negative 9.77% [E56]. Conceded: [E16, E19]. The bull points to a recent ROE of 14.71% [E9] and a TTM median of 15% [E26] as a permanent breakout, but ignores the persistent 3-year and 5-year median ROE of just 8% [E24, E25] which triggered an official warning for low return on equity [E57]. Conceded: [E9, E26]. The argument that borrowings of Rs 163 Cr [E36] are excused by massive free cash flow [E33] ignores the troubling flag that the company might be capitalizing its interest costs [E58], introducing hidden risk to those earnings. Furthermore, citing a stellar relative strength of 94 [E48] completely sidesteps the severe historical volatility of 51.5% [E51] and a peak-to-trough drawdown of -62.1% [E50]. Finally, while the P/E of 11.2 [E1] appears attractive, the yearly operating margin trend remains strictly inconsistent [E29], and price has severely outpaced fundamentals with a 5-year share price growth of 8% against a profit growth of only 3% [E53].
